analysis.title: Market Intelligence: US Morning Update (20 November 2026)
key_insights: Asia equities fell sharply into Friday's close of the week. The report cites TAIEX down 17.5% on the week, and KOSPI and Nikkei 225 each down almost 8% on the week. The intraday index table shows Nikkei -5.1%, KOSPI -5.2% and TAIEX -6.2% on the day.
AI trade concern is rising. Semiconductor suppliers NVDA and MU are down more than 10% on the week and the S&P 500 is 8% below its early-October all-time high.
Risk-off has spread beyond tech. STOXX Europe 600 is down nearly 5% on the week, and the day's table shows DAX -2.0%, CAC 40 -1.4%, FTSE 100 -0.7% and Euro STOXX 600 -1.4%.
Bond markets are now acting as a haven. The 10-year US Treasury yield is back below 5% overnight at 4.98%, and front-month Brent is modestly lower at $91/bbl.

Japan October core CPI slowed 0.2 pp from September to +2.2% y/y, slightly below the market forecast. UK October retail sales surprised to the upside. German federal expenditures declined y/y in October.

Mutual fund positioning at 3Q-end (453 large-cap active funds, $3.9tn equity assets): 42% are beating benchmarks YTD against a 37% historical average, growth funds are at 81% (highest in over a decade), and cash is near historical lows at 1.1% of assets.
Funds remained underweight AI stocks excluding mega-caps ahead of the recent weakness. They are 722bp underweight the Mag 7, unchanged from 2Q, but overweight AMZN for the first time since 2016.
Market breadth improved through a catch-up from laggards and a modest catch-down from the largest stocks, while return dispersion stayed high and helped fund performance.

Walmart: GS is Buy after a 3Q beat-and-raise driven by back-to-school and Halloween, grocery share gains and eCommerce growth. US comp was +2.9%, accelerating sequentially. FY26 guidance was raised and the 12m price target goes to $134 from $132.

Target: GS stays Neutral after a 3Q beat-and-raise with the best traffic quarter since 4Q21 (+5.6% vs +3.7% consensus). Apparel and home are soft, FY27 capex is expected at $5-6bn, and the 12m price target goes to $168 from $161.

TJX: Buy after a better-than-feared F3Q27 on Nov-18, with broad strength outside Marmaxx and the FY27 comp guide raised to +4%. Watch the weather-driven slow start and freight and fuel margin pressure. Price target cut to $175 from $178.
Ross Stores: Buy after a +8% comp (stock -3% pre-market) driven by transactions. FY27 is tracking the long-term algorithm despite cost headwinds. Price target cut to $290 from $293.

Gap: Buy after an F3Q EPS beat but lower FY26 guidance on a soft holiday start (stock +3.6% pre-market). Old Navy is improving sequentially and Athleta is the challenged brand. Price target cut to $25 from $27.

Power IPPs: the group is down 23% YTD after the midterm elections, and GS sees a buying opportunity with a 44% average total return across select names. GS prefers PJM over ERCOT near term. Best positioned: TLN (no Texas exposure), VST and NRG (Buy).

Rating changes: Stewart Information Services (STC) initiated at Neutral with a $49 price target. Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (PAC) cut to Sell from Buy. Var Energi (VAR.OL) cut to Neutral from Buy.

Other notable research includes the Alibaba 2QFY27 review (AI Cloud growth reset downward, clearer path to FCF inflection, Buy maintained), Keysight record orders, the P&G investor day, and Williams-Sonoma's 3Q26 top-line miss.
